messages:
Mira: heads-up — starting ~06:10 UTC we saw a sharp jump in 502/503s from model-serving in us-west-2. Readiness probes started failing and cluster-autoscaler evicted 2 nodes. I’m seeing DNS timeouts in the kube-probes: 'lookup model-config.svc.cluster.local on 10.96.0.10:53: read udp 10.0.2.5:53421->10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout'

infra-bot: ALERT: service=model-serving namespace=prod rate(5m)=24% > threshold 15% — triggered at 2026-03-18T06:11:12Z

Carlos: can you paste the probe logs / node-local-dns logs? also which kernel/mtu/rdma change landed recently?

Mira: paste of one probe line:```text
E 06:09:52 healthcheck failed: lookup model-config.svc.cluster.local on 10.96.0.10:53: read udp 10.0.2.5:53421->10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout
E 06:10:03 healthcheck failed: dial tcp 10.96.0.10:53: i/o timeout
```node-local-dns pod logs show repeated "context deadline exceeded" for forwarded queries to CoreDNS. CoreDNS qps looks normal though.

Anya: we just rolled the RDMA MTU clamp change in us-west last night for dataplane perf — suspicious. tcpdump from one node shows a bunch of UDP retries + ICMP "frag needed" after ~512 bytes:```
16:09:51.123456 IP 10.0.2.5.53421 > 10.96.0.10.53: 12345+ A? model-config.svc.cluster.local. (72)
16:09:51.124001 IP 10.0.2.5 > 10.96.0.10: ICMP 3/4: Fragmentation needed and DF set
```Could be EDNS0/large UDP + MTU mismatch with the RDMA path. node-local-dns sends upstream EDNS0 which increases size.

sre-oncall: quick checks: run these from an affected node/container — if you can paste outputs that helps:```bash
kubectl exec -n kube-system node-local-dns-<pod> -- sh -c "dig @127.0.0.1 model-config.svc.cluster.local +tries=2 +time=2 +noedns"
# tcpdump for DNS: tcpdump -n -i any udp port 53 and grep "frag needed"
ip link show && cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts
```If dig times out but CoreDNS responds directly, that points to node-to-node UDP drops / MTU.

Mira: ran the dig, got timeouts from node-local-dns but direct CoreDNS `dig @10.96.0.10 model-config.svc.cluster.local` returns quick. Output:```text
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @127.0.0.1 model-config.svc.cluster.local +noedns
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```So node-local-dns is failing to reach upstream reliably. tcpdump captured ICMP frag needed on the same timestamps.

Carlos: for a fast mitigation we bumped node-local-dns replicas from 2 -> 5 and lowered readiness probe timeout to 10s to avoid too-fast eviction. Also temporarily pinned the nodes to older dataplane (rolled back the RDMA MTU clamp on 3 hosts). After that the 502 rate dropped to ~4% within 6m. :thumbsup:

Anya: proposed long-term actions: 1) add MTU verification during rollout (eg run `ping -s` probes + check for ICMP frag), 2) make node-local-dns avoid EDNS0 by default for internal queries (or force TCP fallback for large responses), 3) update docs for RDMA/MTU interplay, 4) open infra ticket to run an RUM test simulating large SRV/DNS responses hitting node-local-dns.

sre-oncall: agreed — created INFRA-1427 to track: root cause hypothesis=RDMA MTU clamp + EDNS0 fragments -> node-local-dns UDP drops -> probe timeouts -> readiness flaps. Next steps: controlled canary of RDMA changes with MTU checks, add EDNS0 sanitization to node-local-dns config, and add alerting on node-local-dns forwarding latency > 200ms.

Mira: thanks team — leaving the rollback for now and monitoring. Will paste follow-up perf traces and the INFRA-1427 link when available.
